TODAY IS 2026-09-30. Every "passed" or "expiring" judgement is against that date.

THE AGENCY THIS AUDIT IS ABOUT: Oregon State Fire Marshal
Only this agency. Another regulator's documents are listed at the end as titles only and
are not yours to judge here.

WHO THIS COMPANY IS
  Name: Cascade Specialty Chemicals, LLC
  Industry: chemical manufacturing (recorded as chemical-manufacturing)
  Address: Portland, Oregon
Their sites:
  - Portland — 4410 NW Front Ave, Portland, Oregon 97210 (primary)

DOCUMENTS ON FILE FOR OREGON STATE FIRE MARSHAL — 1
Each is named by a HANDLE — D1, D2 — and that handle is how you refer to it. Nothing else.

  --- D1 — Certificate of Annual Maintenance, Portable Fire Extinguishers (14 units), service date August 20, 2025, Portland Facility
      file: 11-fire-extinguisher-certificate.pdf
      kind: certificate · status: expired · shown as: current
      the document's own date: 2025-08-20 (issued)
      the date that matters: 2025-08-20 (issued)
      site: Portland
      what the reading said it is: This is a service certificate from the company's fire extinguisher contractor. It records that all 14 portable extinguishers at the Portland facility got their annual maintenance on August 20, 2025, and all 14 passed. The document belongs to the contractor, so there is nothing in it for you to fix. What matters is that it is only good for one year. The next annual service was due August 20, 2026, which has passed, and two units need their 6-year internal maintenance before November 2026. Read with site, type, date, issuer and all details from the single page.
      WHAT THE READING FOUND WRONG WITH IT: nothing
      WHAT THIS DOCUMENT OBLIGES THEM TO KEEP DOING (4), read out of the document itself:
        · NFPA 10 (2022) Chapter 7, as stated on page 1; I believe the Oregon OSHA equivalent is the adopted 29 CFR 1910.157(e)(3) — Annual maintenance of every portable extinguisher by a qualified person, with the service date on the unit tag
            the evidence you would expect to see: A current annual maintenance certificate dated on or after August 20, 2026, plus a dated service tag on each unit
        · NFPA 10, Section 7.2, as stated on page 1; I believe the matching rule is 29 CFR 1910.157(e)(2) — Monthly visual inspection of each extinguisher by the customer, recorded on the unit tag
            the evidence you would expect to see: Initialed monthly entries on each unit tag, or a monthly inspection log covering all 14 units
        · NFPA 10 six-year maintenance, as referenced on page 1 — 6-year internal maintenance for units W-3 and L-1
            the evidence you would expect to see: A contractor record showing W-3 and L-1 got their six-year maintenance before November 2026
        · I believe this is 29 CFR 1910.157(f) and NFPA 10 Chapter 8 (not checked against current text) — Hydrostatic testing at the required interval (CO2 every 5 years; ABC dry chemical every 12 years; wet chemical every 5 years)
            the evidence you would expect to see: A hydrostatic test record or cylinder label for L-1 (last test shown as 2020), L-2, and O-2 as they come due
      DATES THIS DOCUMENT SETS (4):
        · 6-year internal maintenance for units W-3 and L-1 — 2026-10-31 (recurring)
        · Monthly visual inspection of each unit, recorded on the tag — 2026-10-31 (recurring)
        · Next annual maintenance of all 14 extinguishers (now overdue) — 2026-08-20 (recurring)
        · Possible CO2 hydrostatic test for L-1 (5 years from the 2020 test; worked out, not stated in the document) — 2025-12-31 (recurring)
      WHAT THE READING SAID A COMPANY LIKE THIS USUALLY ALSO HOLDS (5) —
        a suggestion from similar companies, NOT a checked requirement:
        · 2026 annual extinguisher maintenance certificate — The annual service was due August 20, 2026, and no newer certificate is on file
        · Fire Prevention Plan — Chemical plants with flammable and corrosive storage usually hold one alongside the Emergency Action Plan
        · Hydrostatic test record for CO2 unit L-1 — Its last hydrostatic test is listed as 2020, and CO2 cylinders are commonly retested every 5 years
        · Monthly extinguisher inspection records (tags or log) — The certificate says these are the customer's job, and they usually get checked alongside it
        · Portable fire extinguisher training records for employees — Needed if employees are expected to use extinguishers rather than evacuate
      WHAT THIS DOCUMENT SAYS, proposed by the reading, not confirmed by anyone (2):
        · facility operations: Acid and caustic repackaging lines, tank farm (T-3 to T-6), laboratory with fume hood, boiler room, warehouse solvent cage and drum rack, loading docks, as of 2025-08-20
            it says: "Caustic repackaging line"
            where: page 1, unit table (units A-1, A-2, T-1, L-1, L-2, B-1, W-3, W-4)
        · portable fire extinguishers: 14 portable extinguishers at the Portland facility: 11 ABC dry chemical, 2 CO2 (laboratory), 1 Class K (break room), as of 2025-08-20
            it says: "Units serviced: 14. Units failed or removed from service: 0."
            where: page 1, below the unit table

FACTS THIS COMPANY HAS CONFIRMED, ACROSS EVERYTHING THEY HOLD
Each was read in a document and then confirmed by a person. Nothing a reading merely
proposed is here — an unconfirmed proposal is a question, not a fact.
  employee count (Portland): 42 employees at the Portland facility, as of 2021-02-01 — from "Emergency Action Plan — Portland Facility"

Listed so you can say what is NOT among them. You have not been shown their contents and
must not describe what is in them.
